text: When the sky over Willow Pond turns orange, watch the stirring water. Something down there carries a little lantern home. I have seen it twice in forty years.
Today I caught my first fish. It was very small and I let it go. Dad says that counts. I think it counts too.
If you meet Old Whisker, say hello for me. He took my best hook in the spring of '62 and I have forgiven him.
On foggy days the old ferry crosses with no one aboard. Cast where the water stirs in the fog and you may meet who steers it.
Whisper River is named for the reeds, not the fish. The fish do not whisper. I have listened very carefully.
The Oracle only answers at night, and only in water that is already moving. Ask your question quietly and cast.
I keep the lighthouse lit for boats, but I think the fish like it too. They gather under the beam on cold nights.
There is a crown on the old wreck, and a fish who wears it. It only shows off in the rain, where the reef water stirs.
I tried to paint the reef and ran out of colors by lunch. Bring more paint than you think.
Deep in the cave there is no sky, but the eel still knows when dawn comes outside. It hums then, wherever the water stirs.
The mushrooms glow brighter when you speak kindly to them. I have no proof. I just know.
When the wind blows hard over Sky Lake, the colors come down from the clouds to play in the stirring water. Be there.
If you are reading this up here, you made it all the way. I am proud of you. Now go slowly and enjoy the view.
Club rules: be kind to fish, be kind to each other, and never rush a cup of tea.
Rain is the best fishing weather. Everyone else stays home, and the fish get curious about the noise.
Whoever keeps borrowing my big pot for bait: I know it is you, and it smells like worms now.
I counted the stars from the boat one night and got to two hundred before I fell asleep. Woke up with a fish in the bucket. No idea how.
Every water has one fish that does not show up in any book. Watch for stirring water, and keep the bottles you find.
